item.title: Judge rules Trump administration can’t alter plan to move FBI headquarters to Maryland
item.description: The federal judge said it was improper for the Justice Department to usurp the U.S. General Services Administration’s Biden-era decision to relocate the agency to Maryland. The administration wants to move the bureau to the Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center in Northwest Washington.

item.title: How to avoid 3 types of foot problems that are common with age, according to a podiatrist
item.description: A few simple, consistent adjustments to your daily routine and a thoughtful approach to shoes can go a long way.

item.title: House Ethics Committee opens sexual misconduct investigation into Democrat Jimmy Gomez amid reckoning over lawmakers’ behavior
item.description: Gomez, a California congressman seeking a sixth term, said that he had “made personal mistakes outside my marriage” and that he will cooperate with the investigation.

item.title: Kindergarten vaccine exemptions jump to another record high, CDC reports, as Trump and RFK Jr. seek overhaul of immunizations
item.description: The increase in the share of kindergartners with exemptions extends a years-long erosion of childhood immunization rates, and comes as the U.S. battles its worst measles resurgence in 35 years.

item.title: 60 days after Trump signed a deal with Iran, the war is ongoing and the president is stuck in a quagmire
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a memorandum of understanding with Iran in June. The agreement set aside two months for talks to turn the interim truce into a broader settlement, but the window has now closed.

item.title: Actress Hayden Panettiere was in cardiac arrest before she died, coroner’s office in South Carolina says
item.description: The star of the TV shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” who was 36, released a memoir in May that detailed her life growing up in the public eye, and her struggles with postpartum depression, substance abuse and domestic abuse.

item.title: Supreme Court is asked to hear case on Texas law requiring Ten Commandments in schools, potentially setting up landmark clash
item.description: The justices are expected to decide in coming months whether to take up the case, which is being closely watched as conservatives in Texas and elsewhere work to expand religious rights in public spaces and opponents battle them in court.

item.title: White House races to prepare for new strains of deadly viruses after cutting biosecurity experts
item.description: The Trump administration’s biodefense team has dwindled, and its new safeguards have been delayed — all amid growing concern over AI-enabled pathogens.

item.title: Trump says White House needs ‘military complex’ as courts block his ballroom
item.description: When the president first unveiled his plan for the new East Wing addition, he said it was needed to host VIP guests. More recently, after facing legal setbacks over the proposal, he is calling it a “desperately needed National Security structure.”

item.title: Trump directs Pentagon to scale back joint exercises with South Korea, citing his ‘very good relationship’ with Kim Jong Un
item.description: The president said he told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” joint military exercises with South Korea in the future. On Friday, North Korea had called the latest military drills, set to start Monday, a war rehearsal and threatened to take action against the countries.

item.title: The most common cancer is easy to miss. Here’s what to look for.
item.description: Basal cell carcinoma is easy for untrained eyes to miss, often mistaken for dry skin or a pimple on the mend. While very rarely life-threatening, it can grow deep into the skin, which is why experts said early detection is important for the best recovery.

item.title: Tommy John, whose elbow surgery transformed baseball, dies at 83
item.description: The lefty made four all-star teams while pitching for the White Sox, Dodgers and Yankees. An innovative procedure extended his career to 26 seasons.

item.description: The Democratic nominee is leaning into his background in a progressive Presbyterian seminary to win over faith-based voters in Texas, the Bible Belt’s largest state, but evangelical Republicans aren’t sold.

item.title: Democrats approve 2028 primary calendar that puts South Carolina first
item.description: South Carolina would hold its primary on Jan. 22, 2028, under the Democratic National Committee’s plan. Nevada would follow on Feb. 1. The plan aims to give a bigger voice to Black and Latino voters.

item.title: Democrats abandon deep-red state Senate races, boosting independents
item.description: The Democratic Senate nominees in Nebraska, Idaho and South Dakota — all heavily Republican states — withdrew from the ballot after their primaries, clearing the field for independent candidates. Some Democrats hope that these moderate independents will draw enough crossover support from Republicans and centrist voters who would never back a Democrat to make the races competitive.

item.title: They were on the plane when Trump secretly left. Here’s what they noticed.
item.description: Journalists traveling with the president did not know he switched planes in Turkey due to a perceived threat from Iran. Some said they noticed irregularities about the flight — many of which made sense only in retrospect.

item.title: Luigi Mangione admits to shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO, pleads guilty to federal stalking charges
item.description: Friday’s guilty plea in the federal case will complicate Mangione’s state trial on murder and weapons charges, set to start Sept. 8. Under New York’s double-jeopardy statute, state prosecutors are mostly restricted from pursuing cases if a defendant has already been convicted of a similar offense.
